PS38 — the ARBITER'S spelling of the externality claim. `incoming-gate.ts` reads a claim from an EXPLICIT key list (`EXTERNAL_KEYS`, script/m14/incoming-rule.ts) and `externalTarget` — the key this analyzer has published its externality reading under since PS-B16 — is NOT in it. So every marked edge arrived at the arbiter UNMARKED, and an unmarked external is indistinguishable there from a broken one. Measured before the change at `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts --json powershell ps1 60`: FAIL — 1192 ambiguous + 5877 unresolved of 9911 edges, markedExternal 0. 1,938 of those 5,877 already carried this analyzer's own externality reading.

WHAT PS38 DOES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. `isExternalTarget` is in the list and states the same claim word for word, so the key is RE-SPELLED onto edges the existing reading already marks — `declaredInFile(target)` guard and `externalReadingOf` unchanged, `externalVia` still saying which reading fired, and not one edge added. It is NOT published on every marked edge, and that restriction is the second half of the change: `verifyExternalClaim` verifies a claim by asking about the TARGET ITSELF when the target has no dotted owner, and about the OWNER — a name the edge does not carry — when it has one. The second question can be answered by an unrelated declaration.

MEASURED, `powershell ps1 60` (census `validation/m14/fixtures/powershell/incoming-split.mts --nf 60 --all`, the gate's own imported rule, 978-file corpus for the declaration truth): FAIL — 1192 ambiguous + 3987 unresolved of 9911 edges, with 1890 edges marked external = 179 verified + 1711 unverifiable + 0 REFUTED. The 48 withheld edges (47 that WOULD have verified, 1 that would have been refuted) keep `externalTarget`/`externalVia` and are left unmarked for the arbiter, because no per-file rule can separate `System.Version` (owner `System`) from `[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()` (owner `Text`). Corpus-wide (`--all`, 978 files): 27,694 marked edges → 27,612 published, and 82 REFUTED → 0. Every one of the 82 has a BARE owner — `Text` (Grace/scripts/capture-artifact-size.ps1:115), `powershell` (from `powershell.exe`), `3` (from `#requires -Version 3.0`), and `Test` (ConsoleHost.Tests.ps1:1075, `[Test.User32]::GetPlacement`, a type the run creates with `Add-Type -Name User32 -Namespace Test` at :1012 while an unrelated Pester file declares `class Test` at Scripting.Classes.BasicParsing.Tests.ps1:508); ZERO has a qualified owner.

WHY TWO KEYS AND NOT A RENAME: `script/m60/powershell-mutants.ts` writes four `powershell/externality-*` mutants against `metadata.externalTarget`, and that suite is NOT in this lane's write scope — dropping the old spelling would silently disarm four mutants whose whole job is to kill the shape-only rule this pass exists to avoid. The cost is one 24-byte `,"isExternalTarget":true` per published edge.

WHY EVERY POSITIVE ROW HAS A NEGATIVE TWIN. A rule that marked on SHAPE alone would pass every positive row in this file and fail the twins: `Get-Thing` is the Verb-Noun spelling this file DECLARES (row 6), `Local` is the type this file declares (row 7), `global:Helper` is the scope prefix this file can declare into (row 8), `'application/json'` is a quoted hashtable key carrying a qualifier byte (row 9), and `System.Version` is the broad-owner twin row 4 needs — same .NET channel, bare owner, withheld. Measured on the admitted corpus: the unguarded Verb-Noun reading marks 32,368 live edges of which 7,040 (21.75%) point at a name the EMITTING FILE declares.

expectSymbols.comment: The Verb-Noun LOCAL that makes the guard load-bearing. Its call at line 51 carries NEITHER key, and the cmdlet at line 26 carries both — identical spelling shape, opposite marking, and that difference is one boolean wide.

expectSymbols.name: Local
expectSymbols.comment: The declared type whose construction at line 60 must NOT be marked. No spelling distinguishes `[Local]::new()` from `[System.Version]::new()`; only the declaration table does.

expectSymbols.name: global:Helper
expectSymbols.comment: Published WITH its scope prefix, which is why the scope-prefix exclusion is stated on the target rather than applied by stripping: the name this file publishes is the name the edge carries.

expectSymbols.comment: A QUOTED hashtable key carrying a `/`, published verbatim with its quotes attached. It is the reason the qualified reading excludes a leading quote: without the exclusion the key would satisfy the qualifier-byte test.

expectRelationships.comment: THE POSITIVE ROW the whole fixture exists for: a cmdlet-shaped command the project declares nowhere, now readable by the arbiter. `verifyExternalClaim` answers a bare identifier against the key space directly, so this edge is VERIFIED — verified 226 of the after-run are edges the project itself confirms it does not declare.

THE WITHHELD CLASS, and the row that pins the SECOND half of PS38. The reading fires (`externalTarget`/`externalVia` are set) but the arbiter-readable key is NOT published, because the arbiter's owner is `System` — a BARE name it will LOOK UP — and no per-file rule can tell `System.Version` (owner `System`, names nothing the corpus declares) from `[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()` (owner `Text`, refuted by an unrelated declaration in Grace/scripts). Measured: 82 corpus-wide refutations, ALL on a bare owner, ZERO on a qualified one. `System.IO.Path::Combine` on line 38 is the SAME channel WITH a qualified owner and IS published, so the pair is the check: a rule that marked every .NET type fails this row, and a rule that marked none fails that one.

A RUNTIME TABLE. `env:` deliberately KEEPS the qualified reading where `global:`/`script:`/`local:`/`private:`/`function:` are excluded: no declaration in this file or any other can bind the process environment.

A BCL STATIC MEMBER CALL — AND THE CLAIM IS NOW THE GENERIC ONE, DELIBERATELY, SUPERSEDING THE PS-B22 EXPECTATION. PS-B22 routed every static call on a type this file does not declare to `ownerMemberAbsent` because the generic reading had cost 559 refutations; the measurement behind that number was about ONE-SEGMENT owners (`Path.Combine` -> owner `Path`), which a project variable of that spelling really can refute. THIS row's owner is `System.IO.Path` — a DOTTED name, and no published symbol can be keyed by one: PowerShell class names cannot contain a dot and every variable, function and parameter is stored as its bare identifier. So the generic claim here asks a question the project can answer, and it answers by finding nothing: MEASURED over the whole population, the dotted-owner split moved 1,038 rows from UNVERIFIABLE to VERIFIED with `extFAIL` unchanged at 60. Keeping `ownerMemberAbsent` would have been a claim the arbiter cannot check, on a fact it can — which is the clause-1 debt PSD12 exists to remove. The forbid row below pins the absence so a revert to PS-B22's treatment is caught rather than silently accepted.

THE TWIN, and the row that keeps the mark a check. Byte-for-byte the same Verb-Noun shape as line 26's `Get-ChildItem`, declared 7 lines above, so the declaration guard refuses the mark. `meta.externalTarget: null` is asserted beside it because the OLD spelling must stay absent for the same reason: PS38 adds a key and changes no reading.

THE TWIN through the qualified channel: `[Local]::new()` is the same syntax as `[System.Version]::new()` and names a type this file declares. Its arbiter owner would be `Local` — which the key space DOES publish — so marking it would have been a REFUTED claim, not merely a wrong one.
THE SCOPE-PREFIX TWIN. `function global:Helper` is ordinary PowerShell that THIS FILE declares, so the exclusion is a claim the file can falsify — and does, on this row.

THE CONTROL BESIDE THE EXCLUSION, on the SAME LINE: `global:Helper -X 1 | Out-Null` publishes two calls, and the scope-prefix exclusion must suppress one and not the other. Without this row a rule that skipped every edge on a line carrying a scope prefix would pass row 7.

THE QUOTE EXCLUSION, negative half. The published name carries a `/` and would satisfy the qualified reading, but a quoted literal is not an identifier: this analyzer publishes hashtable keys and command arguments verbatim, so `'Content-Type'` (43 corpus edges), `"Authorization"` (18) and `"it:skip"` (7) all arrive as names.

PS-B21 — `param($Name)`: the parameter is a declaration IN Get-Thing, so the containment is function -> parameter. Before PS-B21 the parameter existed only as metadata on the function symbol, which is why every parameter in the corpus was an F5 MISSING row.
PS-B21 — the same rule through a SCOPE-PREFIXED function name: the owner is `global:Helper`, the target `X`, and neither is a file-scope variable.
The parameter read in the function body, the same PS38 rule as the contains row at line 45, now on the read side. A parameter is a declaration in its own function, so no externality key may fire.
The `global:Helper` parameter read. This is the pair that keeps the qualified reading honest: `global:` marks a CALL external-looking, and a READ inside the declaring function is neither.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE BROAD-OWNER PRE-FIX SHAPE. A rule that published the readable key wherever the reading fired — the first half of PS38 alone, before the 82 refutations were measured — marks this edge, whose arbiter owner is the bare name `System`. It is the same shape as `[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()`, which an unrelated `Text` declaration refutes, and no per-file rule separates them, so the whole class is withheld. `meta.externalTarget: true` is asserted on the same edge by the positive row above the forbids, so the fixture pins BOTH halves: the claim stays, the uncheckable spelling does not.

THE PRE-FIX SHAPE, stated as a forbid because a forbid is the only vocabulary that can say a KEY carries a value it must not. This is what a spelling-only implementation emits for line 51 — 7,040 corpus edges' worth of the same mistake — and it is caught by `powershell/externality-guard-removed`.
A mark on a type THIS FILE declares. Not a mislabel but a REFUTED claim: the arbiter would find `Local` in the key space and count the claim false against the lane.
The scope-prefix exclusion, negative half — caught by `powershell/externality-scope-exclusion-removed`.
The quote exclusion, negative half — caught by `powershell/externality-quote-exclusion-removed`.

PSD12 — the REVERT pin: a dotted owner is a name the project can answer, so the unverifiable claim must not come back. This rarely fires as a 'wrong value' and usually as the pre-fix shape returning wholesale, which is why it names the target rather than the class.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: Get-ChildItem + Out-Null (line 26), Get-Thing + Out-Null (line 51), System.IO.Path::Combine (line 38), global:Helper + Out-Null (line 76). The count is what makes the population independent of the metadata: a change that marked more or fewer edges would leave these seven in place, which is why this fixture's verification is metadata rows and mutants rather than a count alone.

One per declaration plus the class member, AND two PARAMETER declarations: the module contains v, here, p, Get-Thing, Local, l, headers, 'application/json', headers2, global:Helper, and Local contains Render — plus `Get-Thing -> Name` (line 45) and `global:Helper -> X` (line 70), because a parameter is a declaration in its own function's scope (PS-B21). The two parameter rows are pinned individually below rather than left inside this count.
`System.Version` (external, verified) and `Local` (declared in this file, no key). Same brackets, same `::`, same call — the pair is what stops a fix that marks every type reference.

`env:TEMP` (marked, verified) and `headers` at line 65 (a read of a hashtable this file declares, neither key). The pair is the control for the qualified channel. Raised 2 -> 4 by PS38 (pipeline-head reads).

The `#requires -Version 7.0` directive, which the qualified reading marks (a dotted version string). Recorded rather than suppressed: it is a real dependency on a runtime version, and it is one of the 1,711 unverifiable claims because `7.0` carries no identifier-shaped owner.
